name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less, in one of two classes: pedal assist to 20 mph, or throttle to 20 mph. Massachusetts recognizes no Class 3. Defined by Massachusetts General Laws chapter 90 §1 and regulated by chapter 85 §11B¾, both added by the 2022 transportation bond bill (H. 5151), effective November 8, 2022.
restrictions: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals and an electric motor of 750 watts or less
Class 1: pedal assist only, ceasing at 20 mph; Class 2: may be propelled by the motor alone, with no assistance above 20 mph

No Class 3: one that assists past 20 mph isn't an electric bicycle, and may instead fall under motorized bicycle rules (driver's license, helmet, riders 16 or older, 25 mph cap, kept off off-street bike paths)
Riders and passengers 16 or younger must wear a CPSC-compliant bicycle helmet
Manufacturers must permanently affix a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle or motorized bicycle: no driver's license or registration
May use all public ways except limited-access highways posted against bicycles, and bike lanes
Never ridden on sidewalks, unlike a conventional bicycle
A municipality or state agency may ban or regulate it, including with speed limits, on a bike path or bikeway it manages, but only after public notice and a hearing
Barred from nonmotorized natural-surface trails unless the agency that manages the trail allows it after public notice and a hearing
On DCR land, Class 1 may use improved trails at least 8 feet wide; Class 2 is limited to places open to vehicles and bike lanes on DCR roads, and no e-bike may use a natural-surface trail
